```{r knitr_setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
repo_dir = "/Users/haya1/Documents/LanguageModel_Labels/congressional_bills_v2"
data_dir = file.path(repo_dir, "Data") 
fig_dir = file.path(repo_dir, "Figures and Tables/4.4_rhs_results/")
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

knitr_default_plot <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")  
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {  
  x <- knitr_default_plot(x, options) 
  if(!is.null(options$fig.note)) {  
    x  <- gsub(
      "\\end{figure}", 
      sprintf("\\floatfoot*{Note: %s}\\end{figure}", options$fig.note), 
      x, fixed=T)  
  }
  return(x)
})
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_dir)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

  message=FALSE,

# Proxy on the RHS


```{r data_10k}
# Note: prompts were sorted based on the coefficients values of GPT3.5 model.
V.levels <- c("Democrat", "Senate", "DW1")

model.levels <- c("star", "gpt-3.5-turbo-0125", "gpt-4o-2024-05-13")
model.labels <- c("Human", "GPT-3.5", "GPT-4o")

Y.labeller <- function(Y) TeX(sprintf("$Y_{%s}$", Y)) 

prompt_index <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "rhs_10k_llm.csv")) %>%
  group_by(V, coef_name) %>%
  arrange(V, coef_name, coef) %>% mutate(prompt.ordered_coef = row_number()) %>% # create prompt index ordered by coef
  arrange(V, coef_name, t) %>% mutate(prompt.ordered_t = row_number()) %>% # create prompt index ordered by t scores
  ungroup() %>%
  select(V, coef_name, model, prompt, prompt.ordered_coef, prompt.ordered_t) %>%
  distinct()

regressions.llm <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "rhs_10k_llm.csv")) %>%
  merge(x=., y=prompt_index, all=TRUE, sort=FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    prompt.ordered_coef = as.factor(prompt.ordered_coef),
    prompt.ordered_t = as.factor(prompt.ordered_t),
    model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
    Y = sub("Y","", coef_name), 
    V = factor(V, levels=V.levels)
    ) # %>%
  # filter(coef_name!="Other")

regressions.human <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "rhs_10k_human.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    model = "star",
    model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
    Y = sub("Y","", coef_name), 
    V = factor(V, levels=V.levels)
    ) # %>%
  # filter(coef_name!="Other")
```



```{r fig01_coef, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=9, fig.cap="$\\beta_t$  vs. Prompt for all $t$. Proxy on the RHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The coefficients were obtained by fitting the model $V = Y_3 \\beta_3 + Y_{14} \\beta_{14} + Y_{15} \\beta_{15} + Y_{19} \\beta_{19}+ Y_{20} \\beta_{20} + Y_\\text{Other} \\beta_\\text{Other}$ using 10,000 bills, with 95\\% confidence intervals computed via robust standard errors. Here, $Y_t$ are indicator for topic $t \\in \\{3, 14, 15, 19, 20, Other\\}$ and $V \\in \\{\\text{Democrat}, \\text{Senate}, \\text{DW1}\\}$ are the covariates. The human-based coefficients $\\beta^\\star$ (red) were estimated using $Y_t^\\text{Human} := 1\\{Y^\\text{Human} = t\\}$, while LLM-based coefficients $\\beta^\\text{LLM}$ (GPT-3.5 in green circles, GPT-4o in blue triangles) used $Y_{t,m,p}^\\text{LLM} := 1\\{Y_{m,p}^\\text{LLM} = t\\}$, with $m \\in \\{\\text{GPT-3.5}, \\text{GPT-4o}\\}$ denoting the LLM model and $p \\in \\{1, \\ldots, 12\\}$ representing the prompt. In each subplot, the bias estimates were sorted in ascending order for clarity."}

coefs <- regressions.llm %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=prompt.ordered_coef, color=model, shape=model)) +

  # geom_hline(aes(yintercept=lci, color=model), linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.3, data=regressions.human) +
  # geom_hline(aes(yintercept=uci, color=model), linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.3, data=regressions.human) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=coef, color=model), linewidth=0.5, data=regressions.human) +

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lci, ymax=uci), position=position_dodge(width=0.5), width=0.5, linewidth=0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(y=coef), size=1.25, alpha=0.7, position=position_dodge(width=0.5)) +
  
  facet_grid(V ~ Y, labeller=labeller(Y=Y.labeller, .default = label_parsed), scales="free_y") +
  
  xlab("Prompt-Model Index") +
  ylab("Coefficients") +
  
  scale_color_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors, labels=model.labels) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(NA, 16, 17))), 
         shape = "none") +  # merge color and shape legends
  theme.point

coefs
```

```{r fig02_tscore, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=9, fig.cap="t-scores of each $\\beta_t$ vs. Prompt for all $t$. Proxy on the RHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The t-scores were obtained by fitting the model $V = Y_3 \\beta_3 + Y_{14} \\beta_{14} + Y_{15} \\beta_{15} + Y_{19} \\beta_{19}+ Y_{20} \\beta_{20} + Y_\\text{Other} \\beta_\\text{Other}$ using 10,000 bills, with 95\\% confidence intervals computed via robust standard errors. Here, $Y_t$ are indicator for topic $t \\in \\{3, 14, 15, 19, 20, Other\\}$ and $V \\in \\{\\text{Democrat}, \\text{Senate}, \\text{DW1}\\}$ are the covariates. The human-based coefficients $\\beta^\\star$ (red) were estimated using $Y_t^\\text{Human} := 1\\{Y^\\text{Human} = t\\}$, while LLM-based coefficients $\\beta^\\text{LLM}$ (GPT-3.5 in green circles, GPT-4o in blue triangles) used $Y_{t,m,p}^\\text{LLM} := 1\\{Y_{m,p}^\\text{LLM} = t\\}$, with $m \\in \\{\\text{GPT-3.5}, \\text{GPT-4o}\\}$ denoting the LLM model and $p \\in \\{1, \\ldots, 12\\}$ representing the prompt. In each subplot, the bias estimates were sorted in ascending order for clarity."}
tscores <- regressions.llm %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=prompt.ordered_t, color=model, shape=model)) +

  # geom_hline(aes(yintercept=t, color=model), linewidth=0.5, data=regressions.human) +
  geom_point(aes(y=t), size=1.25, alpha=0.7, position=position_dodge(width=0.5)) +

  facet_grid(V ~ Y, labeller=labeller(Y=Y.labeller, .default = label_parsed), scales="free_y") +
  
  xlab("Prompt-Model Index") +
  ylab("t-scores") +

  scale_color_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors, labels=model.labels[2:3]) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(NA, 16, 17)[2:3])), 
         shape = "none") +  # merge color and shape legends
  
  theme.point

tscores
```

```{r data_regressions.averaged}
regression.levels <- c("5k_V_Yllm", "train_V_Yhuman", "Vtilde_Ytilde")
regression.labels <- c("LLM", "Human Validation", "Debiased")

model.levels <- c("gpt-3.5-turbo-0125", "gpt-4o-2024-05-13")
model.labels <- c("GPT3.5", "GPT4o")

Y.levels <- c("3", "14", "15", "19", "20", "Other")

regressions.averaged <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "rhs_5k_llm_human_debiased_averaged.csv")) %>%
   mutate(
     bias_norm = bias_mean/coef_sd, 
     Y = factor(sub("Y","", coef_name), levels=Y.levels), 
     V = factor(V, levels=V.levels),
     model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
     regression = factor(regression, levels=regression.levels, labels=regression.labels)
     ) %>%
  rename(proportion=train_proportion) # %>%
  # filter(Y!="Other")

facet.labeller <- labeller(
  Y = function(Y) TeX(sprintf("$Y_{%s}$", Y)),
  proportion = function(proportion) paste("'", sprintf("Validation Proportion=%s%%", as.numeric(proportion)*100),"'"),
  .default = label_parsed
  )

n_bins <- 30
```

```{r fig03_bias1_llm, fig.height=2, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Bias Density of $\\beta_t^\\text{LLM}$ for all $t$. Proxy on the RHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The bias estimates were calculated as the difference between the LLM-based coefficient $\\beta_t^\\text{LLM}$ and the human-based coefficient $\\beta_t^\\star$, using a regression of the form $V = Y_3 \\beta_3 + Y_{14} \\beta_{14} + Y_{15} \\beta_{15} + Y_{19} \\beta_{19}+ Y_{20} \\beta_{20} + Y_\\text{Other} \\beta_\\text{Other}$, where $V \\in \\{\\text{Democrat}, \\text{Senate}, \\text{DW1}\\}$ and $t \\in \\{3, 14, 15, 19, 20\\}$. For human-based coefficients, the covariates are $Y_t^\\text{Human} := 1\\{Y^\\text{Human} = t\\}$, while for LLM-based coefficients, the covariates are $Y_{t,m,p}^\\text{LLM} := 1\\{Y_{m,p}^\\text{LLM} = t\\}$, with $m \\in \\{\\text{GPT-3.5}, \\text{GPT-4o}\\}$ denoting the LLM model and $p \\in \\{1, \\ldots, 12\\}$ representing the prompt. The human-based coefficient $\\beta_t^\\star$ was computed using the full 10,000 bills, whereas the LLM-based coefficient $\\beta_t^\\text{LLM}$ was calculated as the average of $N = 1,000$ simulation runs, with each run’s estimate based on a sample of 5,000 bills. The bias estimates are independent of the validation proportion $\\eta$, though they were generated in the experiment run with $\\eta = 5\\%$."}

bias1 <- regressions.averaged %>%
  filter(
    proportion==0.05, 
    regression=="LLM"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=bias_mean, y=after_stat(count/tapply(count, PANEL, FUN=sum)[PANEL]), fill=regression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=n_bins, position=position_dodge()) +
  facet_grid( ~ Y, labeller=facet.labeller, scales="free_x") +
  
  xlab("Bias") +
  ylab("Probability Densities") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors) +
  scale_x_symmetric(mid=0) + 
  scale_y_continuous(minor_breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.01), limits=c(0,0.25)) +
  theme.bar + 
  guides(fill="none")

bias1

```


```{r fig04_bias1_norm_llm, fig.height=2, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Normalized Bias Density of $\\beta_t^\\text{LLM}$ for all $t$. Proxy on the RHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The normalized bias estimates were calculated as the difference between the LLM-based coefficient $\\beta_t^\\text{LLM}$ and the human-based coefficient $\\beta_t^\\star$, divided by the coefficient's sample standard deviation computed across $N=1000$ samples. All other variables are as defined in the previous figure. The bias estimates are independent of the validation proportion $\\eta$, though they were generated in the experiment run with $\\eta = 5\\%$."}

bias1_norm <- regressions.averaged %>%
  filter(
    proportion==0.05, 
    regression=="LLM"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=bias_norm, y=after_stat(count/tapply(count, PANEL, FUN=sum)[PANEL]), fill=regression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=n_bins, position=position_dodge()) +
  facet_grid( ~ Y, labeller=facet.labeller, scales="free_x") +
  
  xlab("Normalized Bias") +
  ylab("Probability Densities") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors) +
  scale_x_symmetric(mid=0) +
  scale_y_continuous(minor_breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.01), limits=c(0,0.25)) +
  theme.bar + 
  guides(fill="none")

bias1_norm
```

  facet_grid(model ~ proportion, labeller=facet.labeller, scales="free_x") +
  
  xlab("Normalized Bias") +
  ylab("Probability Densities") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors) +
  scale_x_symmetric(mid=0) +
  scale_y_continuous(minor_breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.05), limits=c(0,1)) +
  theme.bar

bias2_norm
```

```{r tab_data}
regression.levels <- c("5k_V_Yllm", "train_V_Yhuman", "Vtilde_Ytilde")
regression.labels <- c("LLM", "Human Validation", "Debiased")

model.levels <- c("gpt-3.5", "gpt-4o")
model.labels <- c("GPT-3.5", "GPT-4o")

proportion.levels <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50)
proportion.labels <- sprintf("%s\\%%", proportion.levels*100)

Y.levels <- c("3", "14", "15", "19", "20", "Other")
Y.labels <- sprintf("$Y_{%s}$", Y.levels)

regressions.averaged <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "rhs_5k_llm_human_debiased_averaged.csv")) %>%
  rename(proportion=train_proportion) %>%
   mutate(
     bias_norm = bias_mean/coef_sd, 
     Y = sub("Y","", coef_name),
     V = factor(V, levels=V.levels),
     model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
     regression = factor(regression, levels=regression.levels, labels=regression.labels),
     proportion = factor(proportion, levels=proportion.levels, labels=proportion.labels),
     ) # %>%
  # filter(Y!="Other")

alpha <- 0.10
probs <- c(alpha/2, 1-alpha/2)

stripe <- function(nstriped=3, nrow=50){
  start_row <- rep(seq(0, (2*nstriped)*nrow, by=2*nstriped), each=nstriped)
  return(start_row + rep(1:nstriped, times=length(start_row)/nstriped))
}


```

```{r tab_bias1, results='asis'}
bias1 <- regressions.averaged %>%
  mutate(statistic=bias_mean) %>%
  group_by(Y, proportion, regression) %>%
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(statistic),
    "SD" = sd(statistic),
    "Median" = median(statistic),
    "5\\%" = quantile(statistic, probs[1]),
    "95\\%" = quantile(statistic, probs[2]),
    .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
  rename(c(
    "Validation Proportion" = proportion, 
    "Bias" = regression)
    )
```
